summary: Wind facilities over 150 kW that apply for a certificate on or after 2017-07-01 may not exceed 42 dBA from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. or 39 dBA from 9 p.m. to 7 a.m., measured 100 feet from a non-participating neighbor's residence; smaller facilities have a 42 dBA limit, and a 50 to 150 kW facility may instead keep a setback of 10 times turbine height from such residences.
statute_citation: Vt. Pub. Util. Comm'n Rule 5.700 (5.701, 5.703, 5.705(B)), adopted under 30 V.S.A. § 248
amendments_note: Rule effective 2017-11-22 per the PDF header; the Commission's current rules page still lists it as Rule 5.700 as of 2026-10-09. No later amendment found.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: the rule PDF linked from https://puc.vermont.gov/document/commission-rule-5700-rule-sound-levels-wind-generation-facilities (listed under current rules at https://puc.vermont.gov/about-us/statutes-and-rules/current-rules-and-general-orders). A state rule, not a statute. Not in the inventory.
review_note: Opened Vermont PUC Rule 5.700 at https://puc.vermont.gov/sites/psbnew/files/doc_library/PSBRule5.700.pdf with curl and pdftotext on 2026-10-09 (effective date November 22, 2017 on every page; still listed as '5.700 Rule on Sound Levels from Wind Generation Facilities' at https://puc.vermont.gov/about-us/statutes-and-rules/current-rules-and-general-orders). 5.701: applies to wind facilities applying for a CPG on or after 2017-07-01. 5.703(C): over 150 kW, no more than 42 dBA from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. or 39 dBA from 9 p.m. to 7 a.m. at 100 feet from a non-participating landowner's residence; (B) 50 to 150 kW, 42 dBA; (A) up to 50 kW, 42 dBA no more than 5 percent of the time plus a tonal limit. Those parts of the summary match. Disagreement, field summary: the row says a 50 to 150 kW facility 'may instead keep a setback of 10 times turbine height from such residences', which reads as an alternative to the 42 dBA limit. Rule 5.705(B) offers the 10 times height setback only 'in lieu of verifying compliance with the applicable sound-level limit through sound monitoring'; the 42 dBA limit still applies, and the Commission may still require monitoring if exceedances are probable or on complaints. The summary should say the setback replaces post-construction monitoring, not the limit. Citation, technology, state_board and state body are right. No amendment to the rule found; 30 V.S.A. 248 had no 2026 amendment.

state_body: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (permit by rule, projects up to 150 MW); State Corporation Commission (larger projects and utility-owned projects)
summary: Every utility-scale project needs local land use approval (for ground-mounted solar of 1 MW or more, a special exception or siting agreement), and also a state approval: a Department of Environmental Quality permit by rule for wind, solar or battery projects up to 150 MW (required above 5 MW, and for solar only when over 10 acres are disturbed), or a State Corporation Commission permit for larger plants; the permit by rule requires the locality to certify land use compliance.
amendments_note: Section histories on law.lis.virginia.gov (read 2026-10-09): 10.1-1197.5 amended 2025 c. 710 and 2026 cc. 156, 157, 901 (definitions, including agrivoltaics and storage; the 150 MW cap for sunlight or wind reads as in the inventory); 10.1-1197.6 last amended 2022 c. 688; 10.1-1197.8 last amended 2017 c. 368; 15.2-2288.8 rewritten by 2026 cc. 1005, 1068 (see VA-state_setback_standard-1). Effective date of the 2026 acts not read from the acts; the code site shows the 2026 text as the current version on 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl from law.lis.virginia.gov: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title10.1/chapter11.1/section10.1-1197.5/, section10.1-1197.6/ ((B)(2) locality certification; (G) no person may build a small renewable energy project except under this article or Title 56), section10.1-1197.8/ (no SCC review of a permitted non-utility project), https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title56/chapter23/section56-580/ (D), and the DEQ rules https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title9/agency15/chapter60/section20/ (solar PBR when over 5 MW and over 10 acres disturbed) and .../chapter40/section20/ (wind PBR over 5 MW). The 5 MW state trigger comes from the DEQ rules, not the statute; 150 MW is where review moves from DEQ to the SCC. 56-265.2 (utility CPCN) was fetched but not relied on.
review_note: Opened on law.lis.virginia.gov with curl on 2026-10-09 (pages dated 10/9/2026): Va. Code 10.1-1197.5 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title10.1/chapter11.1/section10.1-1197.5/), 10.1-1197.6, 10.1-1197.8, 56-580 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title56/chapter23/section56-580/), 15.2-2288.8, and 9VAC15-60-20, 9VAC15-40-20 and 9VAC15-100-20 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title9/agency15/chapter100/section20/). Matches: small renewable energy project is sunlight or wind up to 150 MW, electrochemical storage up to 150 MW, or a hybrid (10.1-1197.5); PBR conditions include locality certification of land use compliance (10.1-1197.6(B)(2)); no one may build a small project except under the article or Title 56 (G); no SCC review of a non-utility project holding a PBR (10.1-1197.8(A)); SCC permits generating and storage facilities under 56-580(D); wind PBR required over 5 MW (9VAC15-40-20); solar PBR over 5 MW with disturbance zone over 10 acres (9VAC15-60-20(A)); local special exception or siting agreement for ground-mounted solar of 1 MW or more unless by right (15.2-2288.8(A)). Disagreement, field summary: it says the DEQ permit by rule for 'wind, solar or battery projects' is 'required above 5 MW'. The storage rule has no MW trigger: 9VAC15-100-20(B) 'A permit by rule shall be required for small energy storage facilities with a disturbance zone greater than 10 acres', and the row does not cite 9VAC15-100. Also 'every utility-scale project needs local land use approval' should allow for projects a locality permits by right (15.2-2288.8(A)). Amendments_note gaps (not changing the row's structure): 56-580 history now reads '... 2009, cc. 808, 854; 2026, cc. 148, 149, 694, 695' (current (D) text covers 'electric generating facilities and energy storage resource facilities'), and 9VAC15-60-20 was last amended eff. 2025-06-18 (Va. Reg. Vol. 41, Iss. 20, per its historical notes), which is after the inventory; neither is mentioned. Histories of 10.1-1197.5 (2025 c. 710; 2026 cc. 156, 157, 901), 10.1-1197.6 (last 2022 c. 688) and 10.1-1197.8 (2017 c. 368) match the note.

summary: Unless a project is allowed by right, every locality must require a special exception (or a siting agreement) for ground-mounted solar of 1 MW or more and must write state criteria into its zoning ordinance: setbacks of 150 to 200 feet from non-participating dwellings, 50 to 100 feet from roads and 50 to 75 feet from non-participating property lines, panels no higher than 25 feet, screening, soil and decommissioning terms, with any variance only by agreement; localities need not approve and must report each decision and the reason for any denial to the State Corporation Commission.
amendments_note: New since the inventory: 15.2-2288.8 history reads "2020, cc. 385, 414; 2021, Sp. Sess. I, cc. 57, 58; 2026, cc. 1005, 1068", and 15.2-2288.7 adds 2026 cc. 1005, 1068 (with a further version effective 2027-01-01 on portable solar devices). A Virginia Association of Counties memo of 2026-03-12 identifies the bills as 2026 HB 711 and SB 347 and asked the Governor to veto them; the chapter numbers show they became law, but the bill-to-chapter match and effective date were not confirmed from the acts.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2288.8/ (subsections A 1 to 12, B to E) and https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2288.7/. Before 2026 the section only allowed localities to grant special exceptions. The numeric ranges bind local ordinances, so the row could also be read as local_preemption; the reviewer may want a second row. Subsection B lets localities grant special exceptions for energy storage but sets no storage criteria. VACo memo: https://www.vaco.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/CC31226.pdf. LIS bill pages for HB 711 and SB 347 did not load (legacylis returned "document does not exist").
review_note: Opened Va. Code 15.2-2288.8 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2288.8/) and 15.2-2288.7 (both versions) with curl on 2026-10-09. 15.2-2288.8(A): unless provided by right, each locality shall require a special exception or a siting agreement under 15.2-2316.7 for any solar photovoltaic project (ground-mounted, 1 MW or more, serving other property) and include criteria in its zoning ordinance; (A)(1) setbacks 150 to 200 feet from occupied community buildings and dwellings on nonparticipating properties, 50 to 100 feet from the roadbed, 50 to 75 feet from nonparticipating property lines (waivable by the neighbor); (A)(2) screening 25 to 50 feet wide; (A)(3) panels no higher than 25 feet at full tilt; (A)(8), (9) soil and vegetation; (A)(12) decommissioning agreement; variance only by written agreement of locality, owner and applicant; nothing requires a locality to approve; (E) record of decisions and reasons for denial to the SCC within 60 days. 15.2-2288.7(B), (C) send ground-mounted solar on agricultural, commercial, industrial or institutional land to 15.2-2288.8 unless by right. Summary, local_government, solar:1, citation and amendments_note (history '2020, cc. 385, 414; 2021, Sp. Sess. I, cc. 57, 58; 2026, cc. 1005, 1068'; 15.2-2288.8 is listed among the LIS '2026 Updates' with no delayed effective date, https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodeupdates/title15.2/) match. Disagreement, field technology: the row lists solar;battery_storage, but the statewide criteria apply only to solar photovoltaic projects. For storage, 15.2-2288.8(B) only says a locality 'may grant a special exception ... and include ... reasonable regulations' for an energy storage project and sets no setback, height or other standard, so battery_storage should be dropped from this row. The bill numbers (2026 HB 711 and SB 347) behind cc. 1005 and 1068 were not confirmed by me either.

summary: For a permit by rule, a project that would disturb more than 10 acres of prime agricultural soils or 50 acres of contiguous forest (or any enrolled forestry preservation land) is deemed to have a significant adverse impact and must submit a mitigation plan with a 45-day public comment period.
amendments_note: Added by 2022 c. 688 per the section history; no later amendment shown as of 2026-10-09. 9VAC15-60-20(D) exempts projects with an interconnection request accepted by 2024-12-31.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title10.1/chapter11.1/section10.1-1197.6/ and https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title9/agency15/chapter60/section20/. A mitigation requirement, not a ban; the reviewer may decide it is not a siting restriction.
review_note: Opened Va. Code 10.1-1197.6 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title10.1/chapter11.1/section10.1-1197.6/) and 9VAC15-60-20 (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title9/agency15/chapter60/section20/) with curl on 2026-10-09. 10.1-1197.6(B)(7): analysis of prime agricultural soils and forest land is required if a project would disturb more than 10 acres of prime agricultural soils or 50 acres of contiguous forest, or forest lands enrolled in a forestry preservation program; (B)(8): where significant adverse impacts are likely, a mitigation plan 'with a 45-day public comment period', and 'A project will be deemed to have a significant adverse impact if it would disturb more than 10 acres of prime agricultural soils or 50 acres of contiguous forest lands, or ... enrolled' forest; (J) defines prime agricultural soils (USDA prime farmland) and forest land. Summary, state_board, DEQ, citation and technology (the statute covers every small renewable energy project, including storage under 10.1-1197.5) match; solar:5;wind:5 reflects the PBR triggers in 9VAC15-60-20(A) and 9VAC15-40-20. policy_type: this is a condition of the state siting permit tied to where the project is built (farmland and forest), which fits 'other' as a state siting restriction, unlike an incentive rule. History: 10.1-1197.6 '2009, cc. 808, 854; 2017, c. 368; 2022, c. 688', no later amendment. 9VAC15-60-20(D) (no prime soil or forest mitigation for projects whose interconnection request was accepted by 2024-12-31) is in the current text; the section's historical notes show a last amendment effective 2025-06-18 (Va. Reg. Vol. 41, Iss. 20). The row's description of (D) is right; the amendments_note does not mention that 2025 rule amendment.

state_body: Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council (EFSEC), with final decision by the Governor
summary: Wind, solar and storage projects are permitted by counties and cities unless the developer opts in to state certification; an applicant who opts in goes to the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council, which recommends approval or rejection to the Governor, whose decision is final.
amendments_note: 80.50.060 history on app.leg.wa.gov (read 2026-10-09): 2026 c 244 s 1 and 2025 c 261 s 3 since the inventory (the current text also lists fusion energy facilities and adds tribal cultural resource notice; the opt-in for alternative energy resource and storage facilities reads as before). 80.50.020 amended 2025 c 261 s 2. 80.50.100 last amended 2022 c 183. Content of 2026 c 244 not read.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.020 ("alternative energy resource" includes wind and solar; "storage facility"), https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.060 ((1)(b) opt-in list), https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.100. No MW threshold: any size may opt in. The 2023 clean energy projects of statewide significance program (ch. 43.158 RCW, cited by the inventory) was not read.
review_note: Opened RCW 80.50.020, 80.50.060 and 80.50.100 at https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.020 (and cite=80.50.060, cite=80.50.100) with curl on 2026-10-09. 80.50.020(1): 'Alternative energy resource' includes wind and solar energy; (27): 'Storage facility' is a plant that accepts electricity and stores energy for later delivery. 80.50.060(1)(b): if applicants for (ii) alternative energy resource facilities or (v) storage facilities 'choose to receive certification under this chapter', the chapter applies; (1)(c) such facilities are subject to all provisions that apply to an energy facility. 80.50.100(1): the council reports its recommendation to approve or reject to the governor; (3) the governor approves and executes the certification agreement, rejects, or directs reconsideration; (4) rejection is final as to that application. Summary, hybrid, state body, technology, citations (subsection numbers match the current text) and no MW threshold match; that non-opting projects go to counties and cities is the consequence of the opt-in, not a statement of these sections. Histories: 80.50.060 '[2026 c 244 s 1; 2025 c 261 s 3; ...]', 80.50.020 '[2025 c 261 s 2 ...]', 80.50.100 '[2022 c 183 s 10 ...]', as the amendments_note says. I identified and read 2026 c 244: it is Substitute House Bill 2496 (tribal consultation by EFSEC), 'C 244 L 26', governor signed, effective 2026-06-11 per https://app.leg.wa.gov/billsummary?BillNumber=2496&Year=2026; the passed-legislature text (https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/Biennium/2025-26/Xml/Bills/House%20Passed%20Legislature/2496-S.PL.xml) changes only 80.50.060(8) (the chair and staff must offer government-to-government consultation within 90 days of an application, with a summary in the report to the governor) and RCW 42.30.140; the (1)(b) opt-in list is unchanged. 2025 c 261 added fusion energy facilities to (1)(b)(vi). Neither changes the row.

state_body: Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council (EFSEC), with final decision by the Governor
summary: For projects that opt in to state certification, the state preempts regulation of location, construction and operating conditions; the Council holds a hearing on consistency with local plans and zoning and may recommend preempting inconsistent local rules, with conditions reflecting the purpose of the preempted rules.
amendments_note: 80.50.110 history: 1975-76 2nd ex.s. c 108 s 37 (no later amendment). 80.50.090 last amended 2022 c 183 s 9. As shown on app.leg.wa.gov 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.110 ("(2) The state hereby preempts the regulation and certification of the location, construction, and operational conditions of certification of the energy facilities included under RCW 80.50.060"), https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.090 and https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.100(2).
review_note: Opened RCW 80.50.110, 80.50.090 and 80.50.100 at https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.50.110 (and cite=80.50.090, cite=80.50.100) with curl on 2026-10-09. 80.50.110(2): 'The state hereby preempts the regulation and certification of the location, construction, and operational conditions of certification of the energy facilities included under RCW 80.50.060'; (1) the chapter governs over conflicting state law. 80.50.090(2): the council holds a public hearing on whether the site is consistent with city, county or regional land use plans or zoning ordinances; (4)(b) the adjudicative hearing may be limited to whether inconsistent land use plans or zoning should be preempted. 80.50.100(2): the draft certification agreement includes conditions 'designed to recognize the purpose of laws or ordinances ... that are preempted or superseded pursuant to RCW 80.50.110'. Opt-in wind, solar and storage facilities are covered through 80.50.060(1)(b)(ii), (v) and (1)(c). Summary, state_board, state body, technology and citations match. Histories: 80.50.110 '[1975-76 2nd ex.s. c 108 s 37; 1970 ex.s. c 45 s 11]', 80.50.090 '[2022 c 183 s 9 ...]', 80.50.100 '[2022 c 183 s 10 ...]'; no amendment after June 2024. 2026 c 244 (SHB 2496, eff 2026-06-11) amended only 80.50.060(8) on tribal consultation and does not affect preemption.

state_body: Public Service Commission of West Virginia
summary: A merchant (exempt wholesale or wholesale-only) generating facility needs a siting certificate from the Public Service Commission before construction, and a utility plant serving the public needs a certificate of public convenience and necessity; the Commission must find a substantial positive impact on the local economy and local employment before issuing a siting certificate.
amendments_note: Bill history on code.wvlegislature.gov (read 2026-10-09): 24-2-1 last enacted change 2023 SB 544 (2025 SB 763 is listed under bill history but not under signed bills); 24-2-11c last signed change 2023 HB 2870, with 2026 HB 4012 listed only as a bill, not as signed. No change to the siting certificate test found.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://code.wvlegislature.gov/24-2-1/ (subsection (d)) and https://code.wvlegislature.gov/24-2-11C/ ((b) 300-day decision, deemed granted if late; (c) public interest and local economy test). 24-2-11 fetched but not read in full. The statute has no MW threshold. Whether county zoning also applies is not stated in these sections; the inventory says the state has sole authority, which the statute text read here neither confirms nor denies, so the reviewer may want hybrid instead. Commission wind siting rules (150CSR30) not read. Battery storage not addressed.
review_note: Opened W. Va. Code 24-2-1, 24-2-11c and 24-2-11 at https://code.wvlegislature.gov/24-2-1/, https://code.wvlegislature.gov/24-2-11C/ and https://code.wvlegislature.gov/24-2-11/, and 8A-7-10 at https://code.wvlegislature.gov/8A-7-10/, with curl on 2026-10-09. 24-2-1(d)(2) and (4): an exempt wholesale generator, or a plant selling only at wholesale or only at retail outside the state, not operating by 2003-07-01, must obtain a siting certificate under 24-2-11c before construction 'in lieu of' a certificate of public convenience and necessity, and is otherwise outside Commission jurisdiction. 24-2-11c(b): decision within 300 days or the certificate issues as applied for; (c): the Commission balances public, state and local economic and applicant interests and 'may issue a siting certificate only if' public funding and tax abatement terms do not offend the public interest and the facility 'will result in a substantial positive impact on the local economy and local employment'. 24-2-11(a): a public utility may not build plant for furnishing service to the public, 'nor apply for, nor obtain any franchise, license, or permit from any municipality or other governmental agency', until it has a Commission certificate. Summary, state body, citation and no MW threshold match. Disagreement, field who_decides: the row says state_board. Nothing in 24-2-1(d), 24-2-11 or 24-2-11c gives the Commission exclusive siting authority or displaces county or municipal zoning; 24-2-11(a) itself contemplates municipal permits, and 8A-7-10(a) says that after a county or municipality enacts a zoning ordinance 'all subsequent land development shall be done in accordance with the provisions of the zoning ordinance', with no exemption for generating plants. On the statutes, both the state certificate and any local zoning apply, which is hybrid (the inventory's 'sole state authority' is not supported by these sections; I did not find a statute or read case law that preempts local zoning). Amendments: 24-2-1 signed bills end with 2023 SB 544 (2025 SB 763 listed only under bill history); 24-2-11c signed bills end with 2023 HB 2870 (2026 HB 4012 listed only under bill history, not signed); 24-2-11 was amended by 2025 HB 2742 (signed), which the amendments_note omits; the opening clause quoted above is in the current text, so the row is not affected. Battery storage and the Commission's wind rules (150CSR30) not addressed.

summary: A wind or solar plant of 100 MW or more (a large electric generating facility) needs a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Public Service Commission; smaller plants not built by a public utility are permitted by cities, villages, towns and counties within state limits on local restrictions.
amendments_note: History note for 196.491 in the chapter PDF ends with 2021 a. 24, 239: no 2023-2025 act amended it, per the code published 2026-10-01 (through 2025 Wis. Act 247). 66.0401 history ends with 2009 a. 40.

amendments_note: No amendment to 196.491 after 2021 shown in the history note (code published 2026-10-01).

summary: No city, village, town or county may restrict a solar or wind energy system unless the restriction protects public health or safety, does not significantly raise cost or cut efficiency, or allows a comparable alternative; local wind rules may not be stricter than the Commission's wind siting rules.
amendments_note: History: 1981 c. 354; ...; 2009 a. 40 (last amendment), as shown on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/66/iv/0401, sub. (1m). Applies to systems of any size, including utility-scale (the statute does not limit it to small systems).
review_note: Opened Wis. Stat. 66.0401 at https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/66/iv/0401 with curl on 2026-10-09 (page says updated through 2025 Wis. Act 247, published 10-1-26). 66.0401(1m): no political subdivision may restrict a wind energy system more restrictively than the Commission's rules under 196.378(4g)(b), and may not restrict a solar energy system (as defined in 13.48(2)(h)1.g.) or a wind energy system unless the restriction (a) serves to preserve or protect public health or safety, (b) does not significantly increase cost or decrease efficiency, or (c) allows a comparable alternative. 66.0401(1e)(c): political subdivision means a city, village, town or county. No size limit. Summary, local_government, technology and citation match. History '1981 c. 354; 1981 c. 391 s. 210; 1993 a. 414; 1999 a. 150 ...; 2001 a. 30; 2009 a. 40', as the amendments_note says.

summary: Commission rules set the wind siting standards that local ordinances may not exceed and that the Commission applies to its own reviews: turbine setbacks of the lesser of 1,250 feet or 3.1 times blade tip height from non-participating residences and occupied community buildings, 1.1 times tip height from non-participating property lines and roads, and noise limits of 50 dBA by day and 45 dBA at night.
amendments_note: Chapter PSC 128 as published in Register November 2024 No. 827 (read 2026-10-09); 128.02 and 128.03 history shows creation by CR 10-057, eff. 2011-03-01. Whether any section changed in the 2024 republication was not checked.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/psc/128.pdf (Table 1 in 128.13(1)(a); 128.14(3)(a)). Neighbors may waive setbacks down to 1.1 times tip height (128.13(1)(d)). A state rule, not a statute; small wind systems have other provisions.
review_note: Opened Wis. Admin. Code ch. PSC 128 at https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/psc/128.pdf (Register November 2024 No. 827) and Wis. Stat. 196.378(4g) in the chapter 196 PDF with curl and pdftotext on 2026-10-09. 196.378(4g)(b): the Commission must promulgate rules specifying the restrictions a political subdivision may impose, including setbacks and maximum sound levels. PSC 128.02(1) applies to political subdivision review; 128.02(3): the Commission considers whether a wind energy system is consistent with the chapter's standards when reviewing an application under 196.491(3)(d); 128.03: a political subdivision may not restrict a wind energy system except by an ordinance 'not more restrictive than this chapter'. 128.13(1) table: occupied community buildings and nonparticipating residences, the lesser of 1,250 feet or 3.1 times maximum blade tip height; nonparticipating property lines and public road right-of-way 1.1 times; waiver by nonparticipating owners. 128.14(3)(a): 50 dBA daytime and 45 dBA nighttime. Summary, technology, who_decides, state body and citations match. Every section history in the chapter reads 'CR 10-057: cr. Register February 2011 No. 662, eff. 3-1-11' (three unrelated sections carry an added correction note: signal interference, decommissioning and small systems), so the November 2024 republication did not change 128.02, 128.03, 128.13 or 128.14.

summary: Every wind or solar facility over 0.5 MW needs a permit from the board of county commissioners; in addition, wind facilities of 20 or more turbines and solar facilities over 30 MW or disturbing 100 acres or more need an Industrial Siting Council permit, and a county may refer a smaller project to the Council.
amendments_note: Compiled text dated 2026-05-08 read; no history notes in the compilation. 2025 SF 183 (a moratorium on new wind and solar projects) died in committee per news reports; no enacted 2024-2026 change to these sections found in a web search, not confirmed on wyoleg.gov bill pages.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 with curl: the Legislature's compiled statutes https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title18.pdf and https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title35.pdf (PDFs created 2026-05-08, so they should include the 2026 budget session). The compilation carries no section history notes, so session-law sources for each provision were not seen. The wind threshold for the Council is a turbine count (20 or more), not a MW figure, so threshold_mw lists only solar; the solar test is also met by 100 acres of disturbance. The solar definition in 18-5-501(a)(vi) includes "lands for battery storage"; stand-alone storage is not addressed.
review_note: Opened the Legislature's compiled statutes https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title18.pdf and https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title35.pdf (PDF creation date 2026-05-08) with curl and pdftotext on 2026-10-09. 18-5-501(a)(ii): wind energy facility is turbines rated 'more than one-half (0.5) megawatt'; (vi): solar energy facility is a commercial facility of more than 0.5 MW 'including lands for battery storage'. 18-5-502(a): unlawful to locate, erect, construct or enlarge a facility without a permit from the board of county commissioners (exceptions for wind built before 2010-07-01 and solar approved or built before 2020-07-01). 35-12-102(a)(vii)(E): wind facility of 20 or more turbines; (G): solar facility over 30 MW or with surface disturbance of 100 acres or more; (F): facilities referred by a county. 35-12-106(a): no person may commence construction of a facility without an Industrial Siting Council permit. 18-5-509(a): a county may refer a smaller wind or solar facility to the council. Summary, hybrid, state body, solar:30 (wind uses a turbine count) and citations match. Small point: 35-12-102(a)(vii) also makes any industrial facility above the inflation-adjusted construction cost threshold (96.9 million dollars as of 1987) a facility, so a large-cost project under 20 turbines could also need a council permit; the row omits this but says nothing contrary. Battery storage is covered only as part of a solar facility's lands, as the draft_note says. Amendments: the compilation carries no history notes; 2025 SF 183 (moratorium, would have amended 35-12-102(a)(vii)(E)) died in committee and 2025 SF 154 touched only 18-5-506, 18-5-507 and 35-12-110 per web search results pointing to wyoleg.gov bill texts; I found no 2025 or 2026 enrolled act amending 18-5-501, -502, -509, 35-12-102 or -106, but could not confirm on wyoleg.gov bill pages (https://web.wyoleg.gov/LsoService/api/BillInformation?Year=2025 timed out after 90 seconds). The text read is the current compilation.

summary: Counties may not permit a wind turbine closer than 110 percent of tower height to adjoining property lines and public roads, 5.5 times tower height (at least 1,000 feet) to a dwelling or platted subdivision, or half a mile to a city or town limit, or within two nautical miles of an active military missile launch or control facility without military and FAA clearances; solar arrays must stay 300 feet from occupied structures, 100 feet inside the facility boundary and 100 to 200 feet from roads, though counties may vary the solar setbacks. County rules may not be less stringent for wind.
amendments_note: Compiled text dated 2026-05-08 read; no history notes in the compilation. 2025 SF 183 (a moratorium on new wind and solar projects) died in committee per news reports; no enacted 2024-2026 change to these sections found in a web search, not confirmed on wyoleg.gov bill pages.

The compilation carries no section history notes, so session-law sources for each provision were not seen. Owners may waive the property line, subdivision and dwelling setbacks in writing (and the solar residence setback). 18-5-504(c) lets counties vary the solar location and setback standards, so the solar part is a default rather than a floor. The missile facility rule appears to date from 2020 SF 36 (news report, not confirmed). The inventory mentions only the no-less-stringent rule.
review_note: Opened Wyo. Stat. 18-5-504 in the compiled title 18 PDF (https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title18.pdf, created 2026-05-08) with curl and pdftotext on 2026-10-09. 18-5-504(a): no county permit for a wind facility with a tower base closer than 110 percent of maximum tower height to an adjacent property line (waivable) or to a public road right-of-way; closer than 5.5 times height, but at least 1,000 feet, to a platted subdivision or a residential dwelling or occupied structure (waivable); closer than one-half mile to city or town limits; for solar, within 300 feet of an occupied structure or residence (waivable), within 100 feet of any outer boundary of the facility, or less than 200 feet from a public road on unzoned or agricultural land or 100 feet on other land. (b): no county standard less stringent than (a). (c): counties may vary the solar location and setback requirements. (e): no vertical construction of a wind turbine within two nautical miles of an active federal military missile launch or control facility without a no-adverse-impact determination from the installation commander, an FAA no-hazard determination and DoD siting clearinghouse documentation. Summary, technology, local_government and citation (a), (b), (c), (e) match. Amendments: no history notes in the compilation; no 2025 or 2026 enrolled act amending 18-5-504 found in a web search (2025 SF 183 died in committee); not confirmed on wyoleg.gov bill pages (the bill information API timed out).

summary: After June 30, 2025, a county, city or other local authority may prohibit the siting, construction, permitting or deployment of electric generation projects by developers other than Indiana retail utilities, their affiliates and electric cooperatives or joint agencies for no more than one year, and may not extend or renew the prohibition.
amendments_note: New after the June 2024 inventory: added by 2025 SEA 425 (P.L.202-2025), SECTION 21, effective July 1, 2025. The Indiana Code 2026 edition on iga.in.gov, which already includes 2026 acts elsewhere in chapter 36-7-4 (for example P.L.73-2026 and P.L.145-2026), shows no amendment to 36-7-4-1109.5, read 2026-10-09.
draft_note: New row drafted by the corrector on request. Read 2026-10-09 in the Indiana Code 2026 PDF for IC 36-7-4 (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_36/Article_7/Chapter_4.pdf; the URL returns the PDF only with a browser user agent and an Accept header naming application/pdf, otherwise an HTML shell). Quotes: (b) 'After June 30, 2025, a political subdivision or a local authority may prohibit, by regulation or otherwise, the siting, construction, installation, permitting, or deployment of one (1) or more projects within the territorial jurisdiction of the political subdivision or local authority, for a period of not more than one (1) year. A prohibition under this subsection may not be extended or renewed for any length of time, regardless of when the prohibition first takes effect.' (a) defines 'project' as generation facilities of any entity other than a public utility under IC 8-1-2-1(a) that provides retail electric service in Indiana, its affiliates, IC 8-1-13 corporations, certain IC 23-17 electric cooperatives and IC 8-1-2.2 joint agencies. The section is not limited to wind or solar: it covers all non-utility (merchant) generation, so it reaches wind and solar developers; it does not mention battery storage. It limits moratoria only; it does not limit zoning standards or permanent bans adopted by other means, and the text does not say whether a one-year prohibition in force before July 1, 2025 counts (the extension bar applies 'regardless of when the prohibition first takes effect'). who_decides left blank: no state body applies the rule; it limits local governments directly. Also read the enrolled act, SEA 425 (2025), conference committee version (https://iga.in.gov/pdf-documents/124/2025/senate/bills/SB0425/SB0425.05.ENRH.pdf): 'SECTION 21. IC 36-7-4-1109.5 IS ADDED TO THE INDIANA CODE AS A NEW SECTION ... [EFFECTIVE JULY 1, 2025]', with the same text as the Code. The P.L. number comes from the Code's history line.
review_note: Read 2026-10-09 the Indiana Code 2026 PDF for IC 36-7-4 at statute_url (served as a PDF only with a browser user agent and an Accept header naming application/pdf). IC 36-7-4-1109.5(a): 'project' means siting, construction or deployment of electricity generation facilities by an entity other than (1) a public utility under IC 8-1-2-1(a) providing retail electric service in Indiana, (2) its affiliate, (3) an IC 8-1-13 corporation, (4) an IC 23-17 electric cooperative with an IC 8-1-13 member, (5) an IC 8-1-2.2 joint agency; (b): 'After June 30, 2025, a political subdivision or a local authority may prohibit, by regulation or otherwise, the siting, construction, installation, permitting, or deployment of one (1) or more projects ... for a period of not more than one (1) year. A prohibition under this subsection may not be extended or renewed for any length of time, regardless of when the prohibition first takes effect.' History line: 'As added by P.L.202-2025, SEC.21.' Also read SEA 425 (2025) enrolled, conference version (https://iga.in.gov/pdf-documents/124/2025/senate/bills/SB0425/SB0425.05.ENRH.pdf): SECTION 21 adds 1109.5 effective July 1, 2025, same text. Summary, policy_type, blank who_decides, state_body and threshold, technology (the section covers all non-utility generation, so solar and wind are included) and citation match. Amendments: the 2026 chapter PDF already carries 2026 acts elsewhere (P.L.73-2026, P.L.145-2026, P.L.152-2026 and others) and shows no amendment to 1109.5. Worth adding, not an error: IC 36-7-4-0.2, added by the same act (SECTION 10), says the SEA 425 amendments shall not be construed to impair or invalidate a comprehensive plan or zoning ordinance adopted by a local authority, which supports the drafter's reading that 1109.5 limits moratoria only.
